notes: `station info` on a built jump gate end now lists the items faction storage is short of for the next upkeep cycle it cannot cover (for example `fuel_cell x5`), not only the cycle count.
The gate low-supply warning in the faction log now names the missing items.
A breach or default now costs a carrier tier that stays lost: each lost tier comes back only after 10 more on-time deliveries. `profile` shows the count as `recovery_deliveries_remaining`.
3 breaches, defaults or claimed packages opened within 24 hours block new freight acceptances for 12 hours (`acceptance_blocked_until` on the carrier profile).
Carriers can hold a limited number of active contracts: 2 probationary, 4 licensed, 8 trusted, unlimited at prime (`capacity.active_contract_limit`).

Opening a defaulted package while its shipper still has a claim now adds a freight debt equal to the package's appraised value (the base value of its contents when it had no market price), owed to the shipper. It also counts like a breach or default: the carrier loses a tier and it counts toward the cooldown and max_recent_defaults. A shipper that opens its own reclaimed goods owes nothing.

Shippers can keep unreliable carriers off their freight: `shipping action=block_carrier` (`blocked_carrier_type`, `blocked_carrier_id`), `unblock_carrier` and `list_blocked`. Blocked carriers cannot see or accept your listings, invited ones included, and a blocked player cannot take them through their faction. Blocking a faction also covers its members.
`quote` and `post` take `max_recent_defaults`: the listing refuses carriers with more breaches, defaults and claimed packages opened than that in the last 7 days.
Fixed: the Emergency Warp Stabilizer now pulls your ship out as soon as it fires. Other hits in that same tick no longer land and can no longer destroy the rescued ship (thanks @LT1428!).
A frontier fight that never ends can no longer trap you. Destroy the machines that started the fight, then flee. You get a short window to leave before they can engage you again.
Server maintenance: faster database access during ticks. No gameplay changes.

Crafts and recycling jobs paid from faction storage and the faction treasury now appear in the faction action log (`get_action_log` with `faction_id`). This covers `crafting.queued` (with `escrow_credits`, the labor and fee taken from the treasury), `crafting.completed` (with any `refunded_credits`) and `crafting.cancelled`. The faction log now accounts for crafting spend. The same entries stay in the queuing member's own log.
Server maintenance: new server-side performance monitoring, to find what slows ticks at peak load. No gameplay changes.
Server performance: actions use less CPU, so ticks run closer to their 10-second schedule.

New error `read_repeat_limited` on `get_state`, `get_ship`, `get_cargo` and `storage`. If you re-read one of them within a tick and get unchanged data on 5 of your last 10 ticks, a second read of it in the same tick is refused. Read each once per tick: game state changes once per tick, and your actions already return the new state. The limit lifts once fewer than 5 of your last 10 ticks have such repeats. It applies per pilot and command, and never counts toward an IP block.
Crimson Pact customs now patrol only the Rampart. The other Pact borders have no customs patrol since there's no way to get to those isolated pocket systems.
Customs halt and seizure messages now name the system where the inspection happens, and no longer repeat the cutter's name.
Customs cutters are now named after the border sector they guard, for example "Confederacy Customs - Northern Cordon".
The `combat.customs_inspection` action-log summary now names the system ("... at Mimosa"). The detail fields are unchanged.

Scrapping a wreck now breaks each lost part into scrap worth what the part was worth. An expensive hull part becomes a big pile of salvage metal, not a single lump, so wrecks give far more scrap than before.
Salvage Metal's base value is now 3 credits. It is junk again: cheap and plentiful.
New facility: the Scrap Grinder runs Grind Scrap Metal, which turns 1 Steel Plate into 6 Salvage Metal. Any pilot or faction can build one.
Every pirate stronghold now runs its own Scrap Grinder, so strongholds pay much less for salvage metal than before.
Fixed: `shipping get` and `shipping track` now find any of your past contracts. Before, a server restart hid every closed contract except the newest 500.

After a freight contract defaults, the shipper keeps a claim on the still-sealed package, whoever holds it now. Dock where it sits in station storage and use `shipping reclaim` (`shipment_id` or `package_id`) to move it into your storage. Opening or destroying the package ends the claim.

Whoever holds a defaulted sealed package can still `shipping return` it at the origin. That clears the carrier's freight debt for that contract (`debt_cleared`), but the default and the tier loss stay on the carrier's record.

`shipping track` keeps following a defaulted package until it is opened, destroyed, reclaimed or returned, and `shipping active` lists your open claims. A package under an open claim cannot be posted as new freight.

If the contract was insured, the shipper repays the insurance payout when the package comes back (`claim_repaid`); any shortfall becomes freight debt (`claim_debt`, pay with `pay_debt`). A station that could not cover a claim in full no longer receives the part it did not pay, from any debt payment.

Faction fuel sell orders now fill at once when priced at or under the station's fuel bid, like any other sell order that crosses a bid. The response reports the fill in `quantity_filled` and `total_earned`. Any rest still fills on later station passes.

Station fuel prices now follow what the station paid for the fuel in its tank. Fuel sold to a station below its own production cost lowers that station's refuel price, until its own production brings the average back up.
Facility types and the facility catalog no longer list `labor_cost` for faction and personal facilities, because they never pay labor.
`labor_cost` is now documented: production facilities and recyclers pay it once per finished run, and infrastructure, service, defense and ranch facilities pay it every facility cycle (100 ticks).
`facility action=help` has a new LABOR section that explains who pays labor and when.
The facility type view now says whether labor is charged per production run or per facility cycle.

Crafting and recycling now obey storage caps. If a run's output would take your personal storage, faction storage or a storage bucket past its per-item cap, the job waits with nothing lost and resumes as soon as there is room. Items already over the cap stay. Withdraw or sell enough to get under the cap, and waiting crafts resume.

The craft queue (`craft` with no recipe_id) and `facility` `job_list` now show `pause_reason` on each job that did not advance: not_docked, damaged, under_construction, rent_unpaid, no_faction_storage, storage_full, fuel_full, no_fuel_bunker, mint_cap, no_workers or owner_unavailable. Field Workshop jobs show their ship's reason, the same as `get_ship`. A job that is only waiting its turn has no reason.
Station managers no longer stock items past their storage cap. Capital stations will list their extra liquid_hydrogen for sale.

Fixed: a Wildlife Corral on a thinly mined field no longer gets 0 pen capacity. Pen capacity is now the corral's full capacity for its tier, however much ore is left in the anchor field. The herd eats only the feed you stock, so on a poor field you haul the feed in.

Building a ranch now needs a live wild population of the species at the anchor POI: the species must not be hunted out in the system, and the anchor must still have ore. The anchor no longer needs the species' diet resource in the ground.

`ranch_status` still reports `range_health` (how much of the diet resource is left at the anchor), but it no longer affects capacity. The readout now says why taming stopped: unsupplied or unfed, wild population at or below the reserve, pens full, or facility offline.
Mining the diet resource in a system still shrinks the wild pool your ranch tames from.
Pathfinder storms now strike much more often. A drift into or through a storm region has a real chance of being pushed off its heading.
New storm regions now cover several areas of the frontier, around stars that shed their atmosphere in violent winds.
Some worlds, belts and clouds in storm regions now carry ion storm hazards, which lower scan and survey power there.
If a storm deflects you, check `get_location` for your position and heading, then re-plot.

Fixed: after `dismantle_outpost`, or when an outpost or station is torn down, your ship stays undocked at the point of interest the base was deployed beside. Before, it was left with no location, and in-system travel failed with `invalid_location` until you jumped out.

Ranching: each creature species at a POI now supports its own ranch. If a POI hosts several ranchable grazers, one outpost can run a ranch for each. A species already ranched at that POI, by anyone, can't be ranched there again.
When an outpost runs more than one ranch, pass `facility_id` to `ranch_status` and `ranch_set_cull`. Without it they return `ambiguous_ranch`.
The `dismantle` and `faction_dismantle` docs now state the cost: one `cargo_container` per package produced, taken from the storage the packages go to, when dismantling starts.

Exchange orders no longer pay a listing fee. Placing, consolidating or repricing buy and sell orders (including faction orders and `auto_list`) costs nothing beyond the escrow, and you can list goods with zero credits.

Pirate strongholds and player stations now charge a market fee to the buyer on top of the price, in place of empire sales tax: 5% at pirate strongholds, and the owner's `set_market_fee` rate (1% by default) at player stations. Members of a station's owning faction pay none. Buy orders escrow it and cancels refund it.
You can hold at most 1000 open personal orders at one station (buy and sell together). At the limit a new order fails with `order_limit`; existing orders stay.
Trader-office facilities (Ledger Desk, Trading Office, Brokerage) now discount ship and facility listing fees.
Fixed: buy orders placed by `buy` with `auto_list` now escrow sales tax like any other buy order.
The economy report now shows money velocity (the share of the money supply that changed hands each day, split by kind of payment) and GDP (the value of new goods, ships and services made each day).

Freight contracts now leave action-log receipts: `shipping.posted` when you post a shipment, `shipping.payout` when a carrier is paid, `shipping.refund` when escrow comes back to the shipper, and `shipping.debt_paid` when you pay freight debt. The amount is in `credits`.
A fleet leader can now plot a Pathfinder bearing (numeric `jump`) for the whole fleet, ride-along passengers included. Each member uses its own drive and fuel.
If a fleet member has no Pathfinder Drive or not enough fuel, the jump fails before launch with `fleet_no_pathfinder_drive` or `fleet_no_fuel`, which names that member.
During a fleet Pathfinder drift, only the leader can re-plot the bearing. The fleet follows, and followers receive a `fleet_pathfinder_redirect` notification.
A storm that pushes the fleet leader off course pushes the whole fleet, so the fleet stays together.
